pairs.subject: judgeable-spec-authoring
pairs.evidence: src/lib/catalog/contractPrompt.ts:159 The shared produce-prompt builder states the graded-field list as a counted closure (total = described + named, counts interpolated from the arrays), so the spec a CLI authors against cannot silently omit a field the checker grades.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/catalog/contractPrompt.ts:185 Every graded top-level field no requirement tag describes still gets a named line with its disposition (chassis-owned or value-graded); fields on a deferred step go to settledLater (requiredFields.ts gradedFieldClosure), so no read field is dropped silently.

src/lib/catalog/contractPrompt.ts:161 The count sentence is built from the array lengths. The line is only emitted when rest is non-empty, and rest and settledLater exclude each other, so the stated sum always adds up. The dropped-block count at line 212 is interpolated too.

src/lib/catalog/stepSpec.ts:190 Splits two questions that used to share one value: 'does produce declare a direction parameter' (the arity probe) and 'does it actually use the direction'. The override names the second question for the rest/default-param cases (doc at lines 181-189).

src/lib/catalog/stepSpec.ts:198 Names the owner of the field mapping in one clause (UE, where the mechanism lives) and checks it with a parity test. The world-neutral StepContractDecl (line 193) is likewise the only contract source, so another entity's stub values are never repeated.
